Normalisation on a fresh problem

Unit 2 · Week 3 · Lesson 4 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open the normalisation chapter, normalisation-workbook.md, normalisation-answers.md and the normalisation-pack.zip stage datasets. Use fictional data on paper or in a school-approved spreadsheet. No SQL setup or student account is required. Keep original copies. Suggested 55-minute timings are flexible. Explained answers are public.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Normalisation on a fresh problem

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Use the reservation extension of the equipment desk. These are reservation requests, not issued loans. Keep the earlier Loan datasets unchanged. All activities are ungraded. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

2. The three stages

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Recall and partner explanation

Ask learners to recall an equipment example for each stage before introducing the club scenario. Preserve earlier normal-form conditions when moving forward. Avoid identifying the stage from the number of tables or columns alone. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

3. The club’s dependency rules

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked example

The starter has a repeating list of activities for each member. One member may join the same activity once per term and rejoin next term. Each activity has one assigned leader under these fixed exercise rules, and a leader may lead several activities. State these assumptions before choosing a key. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

4. The club’s event key

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Prediction and teacher model

PK is (MemberID, ActivityID, Term). A later term is a new participation event, with its own AttendanceCount. MemberID and ActivityID also serve as FKs after separation. This is a fresh problem analogous to Reservation, not a rename of the equipment dataset. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

5. A dependency to classify

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Guided paired practice

Pairs classify the first two as partial dependencies in the flattened register. At 2NF, Member and Activity separate from Participation. Activity still contains LeaderLabel through LeaderID. At 3NF, create Leader(LeaderID, LeaderLabel) and retain LeaderID as an Activity FK. Do not reveal the complete relations until learners explain the reasoning. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

6. Independent club transformation

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent application

Use workbook question 12 before viewing explained answers. 1NF: MemberID, MemberLabel, ActivityID, ActivityName, LeaderID, LeaderLabel, Term, AttendanceCount, with three-part PK. 2NF: Member, Activity (including LeaderLabel) and Participation. 3NF: add Leader, remove LeaderLabel from Activity, retain LeaderID FK. Participation has MemberID PK/FK, ActivityID PK/FK, Term PK and AttendanceCount. Learners may choose a clearly labelled fictional example consistent with the rules for reconstruction. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

7. A column-count shortcut

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Misconception check with reasons

It needs justified keys, the functional dependencies and evidence that each relation meets the relevant conditions. Four tables can still repeat inappropriate dependent facts. Ask for the ActivityID to LeaderID to LeaderLabel chain as a concrete counterexample. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

8. A correction that transfers

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Reflection and a fresh example

If Term was omitted, a member rejoining the same activity next term exposes the key error. If LeaderLabel remained in Activity, one leader serving multiple activities exposes repeated leader facts. Keep the stated one-leader-per-activity rule fixed. Revisit any dependency that the learner cannot explain independently. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.
